summary:
Occitanie stands under France's national framework, and no trans-specific statute, enforcement series or local incident record specific to the region survives in its sources. That absence is recorded as absence of documented divergence, not as evidence of safety in the department's communes.

Custody is the sharpest documented risk. Article D248 of the criminal-procedure code places detainees according to the sex inscribed on their identity documents, so trans women still legally marked male are held in men's facilities; each establishment then decides for itself between a special unit and isolation. The national custodial-inspection authority's opinion of 25 May 2021 reached Toulouse facilities directly: its visits covered the Toulouse-Seysses prison and the Toulouse central police station, and its findings concern eight transgender women held there. The violations recorded include isolation imposed because of trans status and staff untrained on trans issues.

Placement remained live in the region in 2024 and 2025. Louna, a trans woman detained for opposing the A69 motorway works, has been held since mid-October 2024 in the Tarbes men's prison and kept in isolation since October; her incarceration was raised against the Keeper of the Seals in oral question no. 219 in the French National Assembly, and placement remains under parliamentary scrutiny.

At entry points, trans women have faced questioning of their identity documents in public view. Giovanna Rincon's first-person account in StreetPress of 7 March 2017 describes ten minutes of questioning by French border police at the airport, carried out in front of other travellers.

In everyday movement, accommodation and services, France's oversight bodies record persistent discrimination rather than legal prohibition. The Défenseur des droits issued a new framework decision on trans rights confirming continuing fundamental-rights violations drawn from case files and association testimony, citing the EU Fundamental Rights Agency's 2023 survey in which 64% of trans people in France report identity-related discrimination, and setting out guidance for service providers.

For partner recognition, the baseline is the marriage-equality law in force by late May 2013; CNN reported France's first same-sex wedding on 29 May 2013, performed days after the law took effect.
tangentialFactors:
The BuzzFeed News feature of January 2018 by Rozenn Le Carboulec records no Occitanie-specific event, but documents the national custody regime that applies unchanged in every department, this one included. It reports that as of 1 November 2016 there were 13 transgender detainees in France, and that damages awarded for one detainee's conditions of detention amounted to a symbolic 2,000 euros.

Two incidents in that investigation illustrate how the placement rule plays out. A trans woman from Argentina whose passport listed her as female spent three days in a men's facility in Lille amid inmate threats, including an attempt to attack her with a knife; a second detainee was held following a 2016 protest trial in the capital. Accounts collected in the same feature describe heightened vulnerability to assault and suicide risk under isolation arrangements.

The CGLPL opinion of 25 May 2021 rests on referrals received since 2010 concerning some forty transgender persons, and covers every place of deprivation of liberty. It finds serious violations persisting and records no marked improvement since the authority's 2010 opinion despite the 2016 legal gender-recognition reform.

The national preventive mechanism told the Association for the Prevention of Torture that a further opinion was required precisely because the 2010 opinion produced no marked improvement, because the gender-recognition law and its terminology had changed, and because coverage now extends to intersex and non-binary detainees. Its findings rest on a decade of letters from detained trans people and identify structural problems in the isolation of vulnerable detainees and in suicide prevention.
localsOnly:
The 2016 depathologisation law, n° 2016-1547 of 18 November 2016, has never been written into French prison rules or healthcare guidance, so its guarantees do not structure day-to-day practice in detention.

The CGLPL opinion of 25 May 2021 issues binding guidance for places of deprivation of liberty and recommends financing research, adopting policies against discrimination, and establishing suitable procedures for searching and assigning persons whose civil-status sex does not match their presented identity.

The Défenseur des droits' framework decision on trans rights sets out official guidance for service providers in France, drawing on case files and association testimony of persistent fundamental-rights violations.

Marriage between same-sex partners has been available since the equality law in force by late May 2013, providing the legal baseline for partner recognition.

The figure of 13 transgender detainees nationwide is dated 1 November 2016. Current totals for trans detainees held in Occitanie's establishments, including the Toulouse and Tarbes facilities, are not sourced in this inventory.
